blurb: Yoke in Germanic; Latin iungere gave join, junction, conjugal and jugular; Sanskrit yoga is the 'yoking' of body and mind.
Latin gravis gave grave, gravity and grief; Greek barys gave baritone and barometer; Sanskrit guru is a 'weighty' teacher.
Latin currere gave current, course, courier and occur; Gaulish karros, a wagon, rolled on into car, carry, cargo, career and charge.

meaning: to knead clay; to form, to build a wall
blurb: Dough and lady (the 'loaf-kneader'); Latin fingere gave figure, fiction and feign; an Iranian walled garden became paradise.
Queen in Germanic; Greek gynē gave gynaecology and misogyny; Irish bean gave banshee, the 'woman of the fairy mound'.
Latin fari gave fame, fable, fate and infant (one 'not yet speaking'); Greek phōnē gave phone, symphony and telephone, and phēmē gave euphemism and blasphemy.
